what_worked: Clear thesis that B2B recurring revenue beats vanity metrics, with consistent narrative thread throughout.
fix_next: Nearly every data chart appears fabricated—category counts, MRR figures, and top-performer table don't match the dataset at all. Ground claims in real data.
verdict: Polished template over fabricated numbers; fails as a data story.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: AI shown as 320 (32%) vs actual 197; SaaS & Dev Tools 240 vs actual ~103; Marketing 180 vs 42; Productivity 140 vs 49; Fintech/E-comm 120 vs ~19; categories sum to 1000 ignoring 274 missing. Slide 5: MRR figures ($4,850, $3,200, $2,150, $980) for invented merged categories are unverifiable and inconsistent with dataset medians. Slide 7: Top performer table ('Enterprise AI Agent' $38,500/mo etc.) appears entirely fabricated—no such named companies in dataset. Slide 9: Claims 'data correlation analysis proves' vanity metrics don't predict revenue but shows no correlation coefficients or scatter plots.

evidence.insight: The B2B-vs-B2C pricing power thesis (slides 5, 8) is a reasonable direction but never grounded in actual dataset statistics; the 'popularity ≠ profitability' point is stated as a truism rather than derived from evidence.
evidence.narrative: Slides follow a logical arc: context → categories → revenue → vanity metrics → scorecard → conclusion. However the arc is generic consulting advice, not a data-driven story with surprising findings.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets up the marketplace context and slide 3 explains metrics, but the audience is vaguely 'executive investor' with no mention of dataset limitations, missingness (274 categories, 241 countries), or sample caveats.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 4 fabricates category counts that sum to 1,000 when only 726 rows have categories. Slide 5 uses invented merged categories with unverifiable MRR averages. Slide 7 presents a leaderboard of companies not in the dataset. No actual dataset figures are correctly cited anywhere.
evidence.visual: Consistent template with clean typography and color coding. But slide 6 uses an irrelevant stock image (Spruko admin templates). Charts are simple bar charts with round numbers that look invented rather than data-derived. No real data visualizations (scatter plots, distributions, etc.).
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive: round-number fabricated charts (320, 240, 180, 140, 120), consulting-speak ('Critical Business Lesson'), invented company names in leaderboard, decorative stock image on slide 6, emoji-heavy callout boxes, generic scorecard/checklist slides with no dataset backing.
